component: Trunk Line Infrastructure, Fern Rock Layover, and Stations (Melrose and Elkins Park)
wording: Rehabilitate the Reading Main Line from 16th Street Junction to Carmel Interlocking, including track, bridge, signal, and power upgrades, station ADA improvements, and operational enhancements at Fern Rock.
Reconstruct and consolidate North Philadelphia and North Broad stations into a new regional intermodal hub to improve connectivity across SEPTA, Amtrak, and NJ Transit services.

component: Airport Freight Separation and Eastwick Intermodal Station Phase 1
wording: Construct a separate freight track through Eastwick Station to eliminate conflicts with SEPTA’s Airport Line and enable more reliable service and high-level platform construction.

component: Airport Double Track and Airport Tail Track
wording: Double track a key two-mile segment of the Airport Line and construct a tail track near the terminals to improve capacity, reliability, and service frequency to Philadelphia International Airport.
Construct a SEPTA flyover near 54th Street in West Philadelphia to eliminate conflicts with Amtrak and increase capacity and reliability on the Wilmington/Newark and Airport lines.

component: Norristown Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
wording: Upgrade all Norristown Line stations with high platforms and accessible routes to improve speed and reliability; three are already in the CIP. Rehabilitate the full 14.6-mile line—track, bridges, signals, and power—for long-term performance.
Construct a flyover south of 16th Street Junction to fully separate S-Line trains from SEPTA’s Regional Rail trunk, reducing conflicts and improving reliability.

component: Media/Wawa Line Station and ROW Rehabilitation
wording: Rehabilitate the full 15.7-mile Media/Wawa Line with new track, signals, power, bridges, and drainage; construct high-level platforms at 12 stations and a grade-separated junction at Arsenal to improve reliability, ADA, and service frequency.
Extend double track from Elwyn to Lenni Yard to support frequent service on the Media/Wawa Line, requiring grading, bridge modifications, and crossover installation within available ROW.

component: Major Grade Crossings Along the Media Wawa Line
wording: Grade-separate rail crossings and reconfigure nearby intersections at Morton and Secane stations to reduce traffic conflicts and improve safety on the Media/Wawa Line.

component: Lansdale Doylestown Line Station and ROW Rehabilitation
wording: Upgrade all stations on the Lansdale/Doylestown Line with full-length high platforms and accessible routes, and rehabilitate track, power, and signal infrastructure to improve reliability and reduce delays.

Reconfigure tracks and platforms at Lansdale Station to improve speeds, provide accessible platforms, and reduce freight conflicts, supporting more efficient and reliable service within the existing ROW.

Add double-track segments near 9th Street, New Britain, and Delaware Valley University to improve reliability and allow more frequent service on the Lansdale–Doylestown Line. Build new high-level platforms where needed; final track and station designs depend on further analysis. Add a second platform at Doylestown Station to support all-day two-way service—may require relocating train storage to Lansdale.
Develop a new yard and maintenance facility with crew reporting capabilities between Glenside and Lansdale to support expanded service. Location and scope to be determined through further analysis.

Support implementation of the Amtrak Keystone Master Plan in coordination with PennDOT and Amtrak. Includes new interlocking and pocket track west of Villanova to enable 15-minute service and ADA improvements, and new crossovers east of Ardmore to reduce conflicts between Amtrak and SEPTA trains.

Construct or rehabilitate the Stiles Flyover to reduce train conflicts between SEPTA and Amtrak and improve access to Overbrook Yard. Includes a new Cynwyd Line connection to the shop. Requires coordination with Amtrak and PennDOT, and construction over active tracks.

component: Trenton Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
wording: Upgrade Trenton Line stations with full-length high platforms and accessible routes for faster, more reliable service. Rehabilitate track, bridges, and signals in coordination with Amtrak and the NEC Commission. Requires overnight work or temporary closures and joint planning on Amtrak ROW.

Upgrade Grundy Interlocking in coordination with Amtrak to improve operations and convert an existing unused siding into an electrified turnback pocket for SEPTA trains. Part of NEC Connect 2037; requires further alternatives analysis and interagency coordination.
Add a new southbound track connecting to Mantua Interlocking, eliminating a key bottleneck where SEPTA and Amtrak services currently merge, to improve reliability and capacity through this segment.

New yard and maintenance facility in Trenton—potentially in partnership with Amtrak or NJ Transit—would reduce long deadhead trips, improve operations on the Trenton Line, and support a new fleet; site location to be determined through further study.

component: Warminster Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
wording: Fully rehabilitate the Warminster Line—upgrading track, power, signals, drainage, bridges, and crossings—and build high platforms with accessible routes at all stations to improve reliability, speed, and accessibility.

Extend double track from Ardsley through Roslyn and expand the siding through Willow Grove, rebuild affected stations with high platforms, and add a second platform at Warminster Station to eliminate operational constraints.

component: West Trenton Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
wording: Fully rebuild the West Trenton Line—modernizing track, power, signals, bridges, drainage, and crossings—and construct high platforms with accessible routes at all stations to improve reliability, speed, and accessibility.

component: Wilmington/Newark Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
wording: Rehabilitate track, signals, bridges, and overhead wire on the Wilmington/Newark Line and rebuild 14 stations with high-level platforms and accessible routes to improve reliability, passenger experience, and service frequency.

Add a third track through the single-track segments south of Claymont and Wilmington to separate SEPTA service from Amtrak, enabling more frequent trains and reducing conflicts, with further study and coordination needed.

Build a turnback pocket off the Northeast Corridor near Marcus Hook station, with upgraded signals at Hook Interlocking to improve capacity by allowing trains to lay over off the mainline, while studying other alternatives.

Build a new yard and shop in Delaware with maintenance and crew facilities to reduce deadhead moves and support new fleet operations, with the location to be determined through further study and requiring acquisition of a suitable parcel.

component: Cynwyd Line Stations and ROW Rehabilitation
wording: Rehabilitate the Cynwyd Line’s aging track, bridges, power, and signals, and add a second track plus two high-level platforms at Cynwyd station to improve reliability, accessibility, and capacity, with other alternatives to be studied.

component: Roberts Yard and Powelton Yard Reconstruction
wording: Rebuild Roberts and Powelton yards with modern maintenance and crew facilities to accommodate future fleet needs.
